note: REGIME: a hawkish-Fed rate scare colliding with calm equity vol. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh used his first Jackson Hole keynote (Aug 28) to call inflation 'too high' and put price stability first, flipping September odds toward a possible HIKE (~57%). The 10-yr yield jumped to ~4.72% and the 30-yr to ~5.21%, yet the VIX fell to a year-low 14.35 and all three indexes still booked a winning week (S&P 500 7,711.76, +0.5% wk; Nasdaq 26,402.42, +0.9% wk; Dow 53,559.99, +0.5% wk, first up-week in three). NVDA (reported Aug 26) beat big - $96.2B revenue, data-center +117% to ~$89B, guided ~$108B - but faded as it guided gross margin DOWN to 71-72% on RISING MEMORY COSTS: a headwind for AI-hardware margins and a tailwind for memory (MU held firm). Oil rolled over (~-5% Brent to 89.31, WTI 83.40) on easing Iran/Hormuz tensions, pressuring energy. July PCE (Aug 26) landed roughly in line (~3.7% headline). Rotation risk now tilts OUT of rate-sensitive/long-duration (AI-power, nuclear, high-multiple software) and energy, INTO memory, quality mega-cap tech that beat, and rate-geared banks. spVs200 is an approximation.
whatsnew: Regime this week: a HAWKISH-FED rate scare under calm equity vol. Warsh's Jackson Hole debut (Aug 28) put price stability first and pushed Sept odds toward a HIKE (~57%); 10-yr to ~4.72%, 30-yr ~5.21% - yet VIX fell to a year-low 14.35 and indexes still rose on the week.
Top-scoring names now: JPM (B), NVDA (B), MELI (B), MSFT (B), SLB (B-). Bottom: FSLR (D+), VST (D+), RKLB (F).

NVDA's paradox: a blowout ($96.2B rev, +117% data-center, $108B guide) that SOLD OFF (-4.6% Fri) because gross margin was guided down to 71-72% on rising memory costs - the margin worry, not demand, is the new story.
That memory-cost read-through is bullish for MU (held firm at 932.86 while chips fell) and SK Hynix - NVDA's higher memory bill is memory-makers' higher revenue.
Rate-sensitive 'AI electricity' was hit hardest: GEV -4.4%, CCJ -5.9% (back below $100), CEG -2.0%, VST -1.9% (new lows) as the long end spiked.
Quality mega-cap led the flight to safety: MSFT +1.7%, GOOGL +1.7%, NOW +4.5%, MELI +1.8% closed green on a down-Nasdaq day.
Energy rolled over: Brent -5% on the week to 89.31 as Iran/Hormuz tensions eased - though SLB bucked it (+4.2%) on services strength.

Analyst move of the week: AMD upgraded to Strong Buy at Raymond James, PT raised to $641 (from $565) on a projected 44% 5-yr revenue CAGR. Goldman also sharply raised wafer-fab-equipment estimates (bullish ASML/TSM).
Smart money: a rare Alibaba (BABA) top-brass cluster buy (Chairman Tsai + CEO Wu, >$15.3M); Pelosi disclosed leveraged Bloom Energy (BE) call buying.

Watchlist vs last week: no saved tickers added or dropped (38 saved). All 34 book names repriced to the Aug 28 close and re-scored, with entry/stop/target re-anchored to each name's real 52-wk range; CR's accepted NVDA is +3.5% vs his accept price.
